learning_objective: 🎯 Witness an era of dramatic changes, fierce Rajput warriors, the golden age of the Cholas, and the arrival of new rulers from across the mountains!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In Northern and Central India, brave warrior clans known as the Rajputs came into power. They built magnificent forts on high hills and valued courage, honor, and loyalty above everything else.
In the South, the Chola kings built a mega-empire! They had a massive navy of ships that sailed across the ocean to trade with Southeast Asia, making their kingdom incredibly wealthy.
The Cholas used their wealth to build jaw-dropping temples, like the Brihadeshwara Temple. They were also famous for making beautiful bronze statues that looked so real they seemed almost alive.
During this time, ambitious rulers from Central Asia, like Mahmud of Ghazni, heard tales of India's immense wealth. They crossed the snowy mountains to raid temple towns and take treasures back home.
By the end of the 12th century, continuous battles weakened the local kings. This allowed new rulers from outside, like Muhammad Ghori, to establish a completely new type of rule in Delhi.

fun_activity.title: 🏰 Build an Unbeatable Fort!
fun_activity.instructions: Grab some building blocks, pillows, or cardboard boxes! Try to design a Rajput-style fort that is super hard for imaginary invaders to conquer. Where would you put the secret escape door?

quick_recap: ⭐ The Rajputs built strong forts and ruled large parts of Northern India with a focus on bravery.
⭐ The Chola Empire was a southern superpower with a massive navy and incredible wealth.
⭐ The Cholas are world-famous for their grand stone temples and brilliant bronze statues.
⭐ The 11th and 12th centuries saw new invaders from Central Asia arriving through the northwestern mountains.
